note: Task 16 (chunk e5): weight. The functions of weight.html that its README calls normative: the views (`placeSprite`, `render` with the face-up lean and press, `#screenGlow`, the frame's tilt, sag and tremble, the strain vignette, the level), the floor (`drawFloor` with her screen's light, `legsHang`, `legPoints`, `fillPts`, `LEG_FEET.relaxed`, the kit's `chaikin`), `crack` / `healCracks`, her hand's `say`, the input's `letters` and `typing`, the sound (`audioInit`, `noise`, `thump`, `SFX`), the mechanics (`planShift`, `landShift`, `onBeat`, `slip`, `relief`, `updateLoop`, `frame` with both springs stepped in pieces of at most 8 ms), the phases (`begin`, `exit`), the state (`fresh`, `C`, `ST`, `L`, `size`, `setStyle`, `easeOut`, `pick`, `randInt`, `rand`), its table `STYLES` (the telegraph's lead `tele`, `feint`, `mag`, `announce`) and its `LINES` (checked by `lines`, ruling Q: `cardVoice` `weight.*` by style; her first words `weight.entry.<contact>`; a model-worded `press` cue may take `heavy`'s place). Module wiring beyond the listed functions (weight.ts header): `performance`, `setTimeout`, `requestAnimationFrame`, `innerWidth` / `innerHeight` and `Math.random` are the module's own (the scene's frame clock, the mount's timers and frames, the scene's size, a xorshift seeded by fnv1a of the scene and the run: no rng draw); `$` names the instrument's elements in the effects layer (under the scene's UI: the stop word's pill is never covered; the level's ids prefixed, vial.ts), the scene's reply and input, and the letters laid over the input (`#mirror`); the reply's opacity is written through a claim (styleClaims.ts, recorded as written). The prototype's top-level listeners are the mount's (`env.listen`): Space and Shift never from a field or a control (typing: Shift is a capital), the left button bears her and the right one shifts only on the scene's frame (preventDefault, so the field keeps its focus: the mouse acts while typing), the balance follows the mouse over the document, the context menu is kept off the frame, a key-up of Space or a mouse-up releases whichever pressed, as the prototype's; T is P15a's tap (the card's TAP; weight.html has none, the tap stays the player's). The prototype's scheduler (`onBeat`'s caller `beatTail`, `planShift`'s timing, `attentionDraw`) is the engine's plan: her shifts land on their planned beats (+30 ms, telegraphed by `STYLES[].tele` before), playful's feints are told between two planned shifts (never instead of one), her attention is the plan's beat by beat (`planBeat`), her heavier lean is `run.pressure` (a boundary's press: her `heavy` line). The engine's numbers (`BEAT`, `W_DRAIN`, `RELIEF`) are TUNING.physics scaled to the run's capacity, a shift's cost is the plan's; the strength is set from the engine's gauge as each segment starts; `CAUGHT` and `ATTENTION` are the engine's (`cheatRoll` at the segment's end). `S` is the approved defaults (legs `hang`, foot `relaxed`, shade `shadow`) with the run's style row (`ROW_BY_CUES` for a style the prototype has no row of), the fit of `over` (the art slot's sidecar), her face point and the still form (`env.reduced`, `env.readable`); the contact is read by field (`contactFaceOf`, `herLegsOf`), never by id. The room view is the scene itself (the box is clear until her view fades in: no copy of the backdrop or of her sprite); the floor and the ceiling are P10c's surfaces by finish (`floorOf`, `ceilingOf`; none, or none loads: the scene's backdrop); her sprite in the face-up view is the scene's picture, drawn at its natural size. Ruling B: `startWeight(env, run, { host, core: true })` mounts the core in another instrument (no views; `weightFrame()` for the outer frame). Not ported (README): the rejected legs `x_side`, `x_forward` (`lowerLeg`, `legsSide`, `legsForward`, `limb`, `legsHangB`, `drawLeg`, `M`, `MD`), the feet `first` and `pointed`, the shade `black`, the panel, the start overlay, the summary, the debug readout, the stand-in reply and the `__` hooks (`_weight` is the tests' and the shots' hook). CSS (checked by the shots): the prototype's styles under `.alius-weight`; her lines in her hand at its sizes × her hand's measured scale (R10), wrapping inside the frame (max 40 %, `keepInFrame`); readable mode drops every blur (the glass bed's too).

Prototype only (README: her shift schedule is the engine's plan): the scheduler calls it at the planned shift's beat minus the telegraph, so the telegraph's lead (`rand(st.tele)`, drawn by the scheduler on the same xorshift) and whether it is a feint come in `opts`, with the plan's cost; ritual's side words are her `announce` row's (the word, her left, her right: no line inline in code); out of view (face down, no legs: footrest's form, read by field) the rustle and the creak are heard to her side.
The cost of a shift is the engine's (the plan's `shift`, scaled to the run's capacity), not the prototype's `rand(SHIFT_COST) × weight × pressure`.

Wiring (R16, Ruling S): as a beat ends it is reported: `hold` when it was held (the prototype's slip is the hold breaking; a tilt only drains, so it is never withheld), `uneven` with the mean extra drain factor of the beat, marked `tilted` when the held beat ended off level (`reportBeat`).

Prototype only: the end time (`G.end`) is the engine's; her `longer` line follows the engine's extension (`run.extend` grows once per segment with a slip), so it is said on the first slip of a segment.

The catch is the engine's (`cheatRoll` at the segment's end, by her attention and her reading skill): the shift is reported at once (`shift_weight`) and gives the relief, and her `caught` line, press and heavier lean follow `run.tally.cheatsCaught` (`caughtBy`), so her words never contradict the engine's answer. Only while a segment runs (between two segments nothing is resolved).

Wiring: no audio context yet is not an error (`A.ctx &&`). Her first words are her `weight.entry.<contact>` row (`L().entry`). Prototype only: the summary card and the stand-in reply (the scene's reply is the model's).
